newsitem.title: USA: Italy faces no discrimination on EMU - De Silguy.
newsitem.headline: Italy faces no discrimination on EMU - De Silguy.

text.p: Neither the European Commission nor the EU partners hold a discriminatory stance against Italy entering the single European Currency, European Union Commissioner Yves Thibault De Silguy said Monday.
De Silguy reaffirmed that the Commission welcomes Italy's effort to accelerate convergence to the Maastricht criteria.
He made no direct comment on reports that French President Jacques Chirac said the lira, rather than Far Eastern countries, was to blame for the difficult situation of the French textile industry.

The EU Commissioner, however, stated that "I think that erratic fluctuations are bad for the European economy. With the erratic movements of 1995 we lost 2 percentage points of growth and 1.5 million jobs".
He argued that "with monetary stability we will have growth and job creation, and it will be good for everyone".

"The Commission welcomes the serious effort by the Italian government... The Commission makes no difference among member states... it has no discriminatory stances," De Silguy told reporters querying him about possible negative sentiment against Italy's entering the Euro."
"It's Italy's own responsibility to be ready and to meet the Maastricht criteria in time" De Silguy said.
Dismissing possible discrimination by the European partners, De Silguy said that his "personal feeling is that at the table there are no positions against any of the othrer members."
"Currently, the lira level is in better accordance with Italy's fundamentals compared with March 1995. It is gaining even against the French Franc", De Silguy noted.
